cards.front: Does a parameterised query establish row authorisation?
cards.back: No. It separates values from SQL syntax; the caller’s right to the selected row/action still needs enforcement.

cards.front: Why is CORS not general server authorisation?
cards.back: It governs particular browser cross-origin response access; non-browser clients and backend permissions remain separate.

cards.front: What is mass assignment?
cards.back: Binding arbitrary client fields into internal state so protected fields such asrole orapproval can be altered.

cards.front: Why validate redirect destinations in a fetch service?
cards.back: An initially acceptable URL can lead to a different, unapproved destination with the server’s network authority.

cards.front: Why can an API timeout cause duplicate effects?
cards.back: The server may have committed before the response was lost; unsafe retry identity/semantics can repeat the action.

lessons.title: Secure coding mechanisms: memory, types, concurrency and data integrity
lessons.body:
## Choose invariants that code must preserve
Secure coding is more than removing suspicious characters. Define the properties that must remain true through every path: a buffer access stays within its allocation; a value has a valid unit and range; a user acts only on authorised resources; one approval cannot produce two conflicting effects; an error cannot silently grant authority. Review code against these invariants and the trust boundaries that supply its inputs.

Type systems and language/runtime mechanisms can eliminate or reduce particular error classes. Static typing checks some relationships before execution, while dynamic checks enforce properties at runtime. Neither automatically validates business meaning. An integer can be well typed yet represent a negative quantity, an impossible time or a value in the wrong unit. Use explicit domain representations and constraints where practical.

Be careful with implicit conversions. A string containing digits may be accepted where a numeric value is expected, but conversion can also accept whitespace, alternate formats, overflow, special values or unintended booleans depending on the language/API. Validate the parsed semantic value and reject ambiguous states. For measurement software, preserve value, unit, quality, timestamp and source rather than treating a numeric field alone as trustworthy process evidence.

## Understand memory-corruption and lifetime failures
In languages with direct memory manipulation, a buffer overflow writes or reads beyond an intended allocation. Consequences depend on layout, permissions and control/data affected; they can include crashes, information disclosure or altered execution. Bounds-aware APIs, careful size arithmetic, safer language subsets and memory-safe components reduce risk. Compiler/runtime protections add defence but do not make incorrect accesses acceptable.

Use-after-free occurs when code accesses an object after its lifetime ended. A stale pointer can refer to memory reused for another object. Double-free, uninitialised memory and incorrect ownership create related problems. Ownership/lifetime discipline, appropriate language mechanisms and testing/tooling matter. A pointer being non-null does not prove it references a live object of the expected type.

Integer overflow, underflow, signedness and truncation can corrupt bounds or allocation decisions. If a length multiplication wraps to a small number, the programme may allocate less memory than later processing expects. Check arithmetic in the appropriate range before allocation/use, and use supported checked operations. Merely checking that the original count is positive does not prove count×element_size is representable.

Memory protections such as non-executable data pages, address-space layout randomisation, stack protections and control-flow integrity can constrain some exploitation paths. Their scope and implementation differ, and bypasses or data-only consequences can remain. Report them as layers, not proof that source defects no longer matter. Avoid turning illustrative vulnerability categories into unauthorised testing of real systems.

## Parsing and object reconstruction cross interpretation boundaries
A parser turns bytes into structured values under a grammar. Ambiguous or inconsistent parsing across components can create security gaps: one layer may approve a request that another interprets differently. Use maintained parsers, strict schemas and bounded recursion/size, and reject unsupported ambiguous forms. Validate the structure actually consumed rather than a superficial prefix.

Deserialisation reconstructs data or objects from a representation. Some formats/APIs can invoke constructors, load types or execute behaviour during reconstruction. Do not use a code-capable object deserialiser for untrusted input simply because the file has a familiar extension. Prefer a constrained data format and explicit schema when the requirement is data exchange. Signing a file helps only if the signer, content scope and key authority are appropriate; it does not make arbitrary authorised code harmless.

Dynamic evaluation and template engines similarly turn data into instructions under their language. Use fixed code paths and constrained data APIs instead of evaluating user-supplied expressions with broad runtime authority. If an expression language is a real requirement, design a limited grammar, resource bounds and isolated permissions with specialist review. A blacklist of a few function names rarely establishes a complete sandbox.

Object-oriented encapsulation can help keep state changes behind controlled methods, but access modifiers are not an external security boundary against every runtime or administrator. Inheritance and polymorphism can alter behaviour in ways that bypass assumptions in a parent class. Review overridden methods, extension/plugin authority and invariants across interfaces. A design pattern is useful only if the actual callers and implementation preserve its properties.

## Concurrency changes what a check proves
A race condition occurs when behaviour depends on an uncontrolled ordering of concurrent activities. A check that an object is available can become stale before it is modified. Time-of-check/time-of-use defects are a particular form: the resource or authority changes between validation and use. Locks, transactions, conditional updates, version checks or atomic operations may address different cases; choose the mechanism that enforces the actual invariant.

For a synthetic reservation, an atomic conditional update can express 'decrement remaining capacity only when it is positive' and verify the affected-row count. A read-then-write sequence without suitable isolation can let two workers both observe one remaining unit and each allocate it. A mutex in one process does not coordinate another process or service unless the design explicitly shares the enforcement.

Database transactions provide properties under a selected isolation and durability configuration. ACID does not mean every business rule is automatically encoded. Use constraints and appropriate transaction logic to enforce uniqueness, referential integrity and permitted state transitions. Eventual consistency can be suitable for some observations but unsuitable for an invariant requiring an authoritative serial decision. State the model and failure consequences.

Deadlocks and resource starvation also affect availability. Establish consistent locking order where appropriate, bounded waits, cancellation and recovery behaviour. A timeout during a transaction or distributed operation leaves a state question that needs resolution; do not blindly assume nothing committed. Log correlation identifiers and preserve enough context to reconcile without exposing secrets.

## Data security includes inference and integrity semantics
Relational normalisation reduces certain redundancy and update anomalies, but it does not automatically enforce confidentiality. Database views, row/column permissions and stored procedures can support access boundaries when correctly designed. A privileged export or backup path may bypass those boundaries. Review the effective authority of application and administrative accounts.

Aggregates can reveal sensitive information through small groups or repeated queries. Removing names does not guarantee anonymity if context or linkage identifies a person. Query controls, suppression, privacy-preserving methods and purpose limits need analysis against the actual threat and data. The earlier asset-security chapters explain lifecycle responsibilities; here the coding task is to ensure the implemented query/output matches those requirements.

Integrity means more than a checksum. A signed measurement with the wrong unit or a valid record assigned to the wrong asset can be authentic yet operationally misleading. Enforce schema, units, asset binding, quality and time requirements, and preserve unknown/invalid states explicitly. Converting a failed read to zero can make a control or report interpret missing data as a legitimate measurement.

## Errors, logs and cleanup are security behaviour
Error handling should preserve the required authority and state. A permission-service exception must not default to permit merely to avoid user-facing failures. For a critical physical function, the approved degraded mode needs explicit bounded behaviour rather than an accidental coding fallback. Distinguish denial, unavailable, unknown and successful outcomes so operators and calling services can respond correctly.

Return useful bounded errors to clients while retaining protected diagnostic evidence for authorised investigation. Stack traces, SQL statements, filesystem paths, access tokens and secrets can expose sensitive implementation details. Logs can also become an injection/output problem when untrusted text is rendered or used in downstream queries. Structure events, escape/encode at the appropriate sink and limit unnecessary sensitive content.

Resource cleanup must work on success, error, cancellation and timeout. Leaked file handles, connections, locks or memory can exhaust a service even without a memory corruption exploit. Use language/framework lifetime constructs and test failure paths. Temporary files, caches and crash dumps can retain secrets beyond the normal request lifecycle; include permissions, retention and sanitisation appropriate to the platform.

## Review and test against independently derived expectations
Code review should connect a change to its requirement, trust boundary and failure model. Look for unsafe interpretation, unchecked authority, ambiguous data, resource growth and state-transition defects. Static analysis, linters, dependency checks, fuzzing and dynamic tests can support the review but cannot replace the reasoning about business meaning.

Use boundary values, malformed structures, concurrent operations, cancellation and dependency failure tests with expected results derived from the invariant. Property-based tests can exercise many input combinations around a stated property; fuzzing explores unexpected inputs and behaviour. Retain failing cases and regression tests after repair. A test that repeats the same implementation formula can share its mistake, so validate outcomes through independent models or hand-worked examples where useful.

worked_examples.title: Capacity check races
worked_examples.scenario: A synthetic pool has one free unit. Two workers both read remaining=1, then each writes remaining=0 and reports a successful allocation.
worked_examples.solution: The final counter looks nonnegative but two units were allocated. Enforce the allocation invariant atomically with suitable shared transaction/conditional logic and verify success from the committed result. A per-worker read check does not coordinate the concurrent operations.

worked_examples.title: A failed measurement becomes a false zero
worked_examples.scenario: A synthetic parser catches every exception and returns 0. A dashboard labels the result as a valid 0 kW reading with the current time.
worked_examples.solution: The error path manufactures a valid measurement and freshness claim. Preserve an explicit invalid/unknown quality state with source/time evidence, and let downstream logic follow the approved failure design. Zero is a possible value, not a universal error code.

guided_practice.prompt: A function checks that a path is inside an approved directory, but another actor replaces a link before the file is opened. Which invariant must the implementation enforce?
guided_practice.hint: The resource actually used must remain the authorised resource, not merely have passed an earlier string check.
guided_practice.solution: Use appropriate platform operations and authority constraints to bind validation and use to the intended resource, accounting for links and concurrent changes. Test the race in an isolated model. Repeating the same pre-open string comparison does not by itself establish atomicity.

independent_task.environment: analytical; approved organisational evidence where available
independent_task.brief: Implement and review bounded synthetic data and state transitions in the offline casebook.
deliverables: Failure quality, cleanup and sensitive-log checks
acceptance_criteria: Derive expected results from explicit invariants.
Do not treat memory safety as complete application security.
Preserve missing/invalid states rather than silently inventing valid data.
independent_task.limitations: Supplied scenarios are synthetic. A written analysis demonstrates reasoning; organisational effectiveness, legal applicability and operational authority require actual evidence and appropriate review.

lessons.title: Acquired software, build provenance and sustained supply-chain assurance
lessons.body:
## Acquisition is an engineering and governance decision
Software can be built internally, purchased as a commercial package, assembled from open-source components or consumed as a managed/cloud service. These choices distribute implementation and operational responsibilities differently. None is inherently trustworthy because of its acquisition label. Define the required function, data handling, security properties, integration, support, recovery and retirement needs before comparing products.

A commercial supplier may provide support, documentation and contractual commitments while retaining control of source or updates. Open-source availability can support inspection and adaptation, but visibility alone does not prove that qualified review occurred or that maintainers can respond to a defect. Managed services shift more operational implementation to a provider while leaving customer identities, configuration, data and risk decisions. Assess the actual responsibilities and evidence.

Acquisition requirements should include supported platforms and versions, secure configuration, identity integration, logging/export, vulnerability reporting, patch/update practices, compatibility, incident cooperation and exit/recovery. Contracts and licences require the appropriate legal/procurement review for the jurisdiction and use. A technical security assessment does not decide every licence obligation, but it should identify dependencies and intended redistribution or modification that need review.

## Inventory the software that actually runs
A software bill of materials describes components and relationships under a defined format and generation method. It can support vulnerability analysis and dependency management, but its usefulness depends on completeness, identifiers, versions, relationships and association with the actual artifact. A source-repository dependency list may differ from a shipped binary or container after build-time resolution and packaging.

Transitive dependencies matter: a small library can bring many other components. Runtime plugins, dynamically downloaded packages, operating-system components and externally hosted scripts can add dependencies after the initial build. Compare declared, built, deployed and loaded state. A bill of materials that omits the affected runtime component cannot support a complete exposure decision.

An SBOM is an inventory, not a vulnerability-free certificate or a licence-compliance verdict. Link it to current vulnerability information, configuration, reachability, feature use and available mitigations. Version matching is an initial hypothesis: vendor backports, build flags or disabled features can affect applicability. Preserve the evidence behind affected/not-affected conclusions and update them when configuration or new information changes.

Vulnerability exploitability statements can communicate an assessed relationship between a component issue and a product context. Treat them as claims with issuer, scope, evidence and lifecycle, not a universal exemption. A supplier statement for one build or configuration may not cover a modified deployment. An unavailable exploitation proof does not automatically mean no risk; assess plausible paths and consequences under the intended use.

## Protect dependency resolution and update paths
Package names and versions are resolved through repositories, registries, mirrors and local caches. An attacker can exploit ambiguous namespaces, untrusted sources or compromised publishing authority without modifying the organisation's main source repository. Control approved registries and resolution rules, constrain dependency versions under policy and verify artifact identity through a trusted process.

A lock file can improve repeatability by recording resolved versions and sometimes integrity information. It does not guarantee that the selected package is safe or that every build input is fixed. Compilers, base images, scripts, environment variables and network-fetched resources can still change outputs. Review the complete build dependency graph and the authority that can alter it.

Updates need authenticated origin and appropriate integrity checks. A signature proves a relationship to a signing key under its scheme; the organisation still must trust the publisher, protect the signing operation and assess the artifact's suitability. A compromised legitimate publisher can sign malicious content. Use provenance, review, staged deployment, monitoring and recovery to address different parts of that risk.

Rollback protections and downgrade policies matter for security updates. Reverting to a previously vulnerable version may restore functionality while reintroducing exposure. Define when rollback is permitted, what compensating measures and authority are required and how the forward repair is completed. A signed old artifact is not automatically acceptable forever.

## Provenance connects artifacts to a build process
Build provenance records information about how an artifact was produced, such as source, build process, inputs and builder identity under the selected framework. Its value depends on trustworthy generation and protection. A developer-written text file claiming a clean build is weaker than appropriately protected evidence from an independently constrained build service.

Verify both the provenance statement and its relationship to the artifact. Check the subject digest, trusted builder/issuer, expected source and build parameters, and the policy for accepted evidence. A valid signature over provenance for artifact A does not establish anything about unrelated artifact B. A trustworthy statement can also reveal that the artifact was built from an unapproved source, in which case the correct action is rejection under policy.

Reproducible builds aim to produce the same output from defined inputs and environment. They can help detect unexplained differences, but reproducibility alone does not make the source benign. A hermetic build constrains dependence on undeclared external inputs under its model. These are related but distinct properties. Explain what the particular build process actually controls and which environmental or toolchain assumptions remain.

Build and signing services need least privilege, isolation, protected administration, tamper-resistant evidence and incident recovery. A runner that can edit its own logs, retrieve every signing key and publish arbitrary releases is a large trust concentration. Limit cross-project access and separate untrusted contribution tests from release operations. Review the identities that change pipeline definitions and policy, not only those that press deploy.

## Assess third-party and cloud services through scoped evidence
Supplier questionnaires, audits, evaluation reports and penetration tests can inform an assessment. Read their dates, scope, tested configurations, exceptions, methods and customer responsibilities. A report about the provider's corporate controls may not test the customer-facing API configuration used by the organisation. Map actual evidence to requirements and identify what must be verified locally.

For a managed service, examine data location and flows, administrative/support access, tenant isolation, logging, key control, backup/recovery, availability dependencies and export/exit. A contractual availability target does not establish that the customer's identity, network and operational processes can meet their recovery objective. Test recoverability and interoperability through approved methods and retain a realistic exit plan.

Acquired software also changes maintenance burden. Identify end-of-support dates, update compatibility, required skills, licensing access and the ability to recover if the supplier or repository becomes unavailable. A component that is free to download can still impose significant engineering and operational costs. Ownership must persist after the initial project budget ends.

## AI models and generated code add artifacts and trust paths
AI-enabled software includes model weights, training/fine-tuning data, prompts, retrieval sources, evaluation sets, runtime libraries and tool connections. Inventory these artifacts and their provenance, permissions and update lifecycle. A model file can be intellectual property and may carry risks through unsafe loading formats or untrusted supporting code. Treat the complete package and runtime, not only a model name, as the acquired system.

Data poisoning changes training or retrieval material in a way that can influence behaviour. Prompt injection attempts to turn untrusted content into instructions or authority in an application workflow. Model extraction and privacy inference concern information that can be learned through access or outputs. These risks need different tests and controls; a single generic AI score does not establish safety or security for every use.

Generated code is a proposal that requires the same requirements, review, testing, dependency and provenance discipline as other code. It may contain plausible but incorrect APIs, insecure defaults, fabricated assumptions or copied patterns whose use needs review. Do not grant generated output automatic release authority. Use constrained build/test environments and validate the resulting behaviour against independent expectations.

AI-assisted detection or triage can help prioritise evidence, but its output can be wrong or manipulated. Preserve original observations, uncertainty and review of consequential actions. An explanation can aid investigation without proving the model's internal reasoning or the correctness of its conclusion. The programme's broader agent/OT chapters require explicit read/write boundaries and process authority before operational changes.

## Sustain assurance after procurement
Maintain vulnerability intake, supplier contact paths, asset applicability, remediation decisions, compensating controls and verification. A fix should be checked in the actual deployment and against the original defect and regression risks. Track unresolved exceptions and support limitations with owners and review triggers. Reassess after significant integration, supplier, ownership or threat changes.

At retirement, remove software, credentials, service accounts, trust relationships, scheduled jobs and external integrations according to the approved plan. Preserve required evidence and data in usable formats and verify sanitisation or controlled retention. An uninstalled application may leave agents, keys, cloud resources or browser extensions behind. End-to-end software assurance includes the state left after the product is no longer actively used.

worked_examples.title: The inventory does not match the deployed artifact
worked_examples.scenario: A synthetic SBOM lists library version 4.1 from the repository, but the shipped container digest includes 4.0 through a cached build layer.
worked_examples.solution: Use artifact-bound inventory and inspect the actual built/deployed content. Determine issue applicability for the loaded version and correct the build/cache/inventory process. A repository declaration is not proof of the final artifact’s component set.

worked_examples.title: Valid provenance for an unacceptable source
worked_examples.scenario: A synthetic provenance signature validates under the trusted builder and matches the artifact digest, but identifies an unapproved fork and a disabled test stage.
worked_examples.solution: The evidence may be authentic while proving the build fails acceptance policy. Reject or route the exception through the authorised process; do not equate valid provenance with automatic approval. Trustworthy evidence helps evaluate the actual source and process.

guided_practice.prompt: A supplier says a vulnerability is not applicable to its standard build. The customer enables an optional plugin and changes the exposed interface. What should be assessed?
guided_practice.hint: Applicability statements have configuration and product scope.
guided_practice.solution: Compare the supplier claim’s assumptions with the modified deployment, including component version, feature use, reachability and consequence. Obtain or produce appropriate evidence for the difference and retain a bounded treatment decision. Do not transfer a scoped statement automatically to an altered system.

independent_task.environment: analytical; approved organisational evidence where available
independent_task.brief: Assess a synthetic acquired software/AI integration through its full lifecycle.
acceptance_criteria: Treat SBOM and provenance as scoped evidence, not automatic safety approval.
Verify built/deployed/loaded state and modified configurations.
Require review and tests before generated code or model output gains operational authority.
independent_task.limitations: Supplied scenarios are synthetic. A written analysis demonstrates reasoning; organisational effectiveness, legal applicability and operational authority require actual evidence and appropriate review.

NIST SP 800-160 Vol.1 Rev.1 systems security engineering

cards.front: What does an SBOM establish narrowly?
cards.back: A component inventory under its stated generation scope; it does not prove absence of vulnerabilities or complete licence compliance.

cards.front: Why bind provenance to an artifact digest?
cards.back: A valid statement about one artifact must not be accepted as evidence for different content.

cards.front: Reproducible versus hermetic builds?
cards.back: Reproducibility concerns matching outputs from defined inputs; hermeticity constrains undeclared external build dependencies under the model.

cards.front: Can a validly signed update still be unsafe?
cards.back: Yes. The publisher or signing operation can be compromised, or the authentic update can violate deployment requirements.

cards.front: How should generated code be treated?
cards.back: As proposed code requiring normal requirements, review, dependency analysis, testing and controlled release authority.

questions.prompt: A network engineer can implement a requested exposure but its potential loss exceeds the service owner’s delegated limit. What should happen before implementation?
options: Have the service owner split it into smaller change tickets
Let the engineer accept it because the change is technically reversible
Escalate acceptance to the authority that can accept that loss
explanations: Administrative ticket splitting does not change the material risk and defeats the governance limit.
Reversibility does not remove the consequence during exposure or confer business authority.
Delegation is defined by the aggregate exposure; the competent authority must decide treatment or acceptance.

questions.prompt: Which document statement is most suitable as a measurable privileged-access standard?
options: Protect administrative access appropriately
Production administrator privileges expire at the approved task end time
Open the access console and click Add Role
explanations: This is broad policy intent without an acceptance condition.
It specifies a mandatory observable property that implementation and assessment can verify.
This is a product-specific execution step, suitable for a procedure rather than the governing standard.

questions.prompt: A control dashboard counts installed agents. Which additional evidence best tests the intended detection outcome?
options: A relevant test event is collected, detected and investigated within the agreed objective
The supplier recognises the product as an industry leader
The installer completed without errors on the deployment server
explanations: This traces the full detection service rather than a deployment activity.
Market position is not evidence of the organisation’s control performance.
Installer success does not establish telemetry or response effectiveness.

questions.prompt: Which paired actions best illustrate diligence followed by care in supplier onboarding?
options: Investigate support and security dependencies, then implement and verify the required safeguards
Publish a supplier policy, then count its downloads
Purchase insurance, then assume the supplier risk has disappeared
explanations: The first gathers decision evidence; the second implements reasonable protection based on it.
Publication and readership do not establish supplier evaluation or safeguards.
Insurance may transfer part of financial loss but leaves operational and other residual consequences.

questions.prompt: A legacy gateway has an MFA exception protected by a jump host. Which finding most directly invalidates the compensating design?
options: The exception was approved by the designated service owner
A vendor tunnel reaches the gateway without traversing the jump host
The gateway interface still displays a password field
explanations: Correct approval establishes authority, although it cannot by itself establish technical effectiveness.
The bypass removes the control from an allowed access path, leaving the original exposure.
A legacy password field can exist behind a properly enforced stronger access boundary.

questions.prompt: A policy exception has an owner and approval but no end condition. What is the most significant governance defect?
options: The exception automatically becomes a new enterprise policy
The organisation cannot distinguish a temporary deviation from an indefinitely accepted control gap
The technical control must immediately stop functioning
explanations: An exception does not automatically amend policy for unrelated assets.
A review/expiry and closure condition create accountability for continued exposure.
The governance defect does not imply a particular technical state.

questions.prompt: An assessor discovers that a failover was never executed although the report calls it tested. What is the appropriate immediate professional action?
options: Correct the assurance claim and escalate the material evidence gap through the review process
Run an unapproved failover during peak service to make the report true
Leave the wording because the design appears technically sound
explanations: Truthful reporting and appropriate escalation preserve evidence and allow a justified decision.
A surprise production test can create harm and is not authorised by the reporting problem.
Design plausibility does not support a claim of observed execution.

questions.prompt: During an acquisition, which decision most directly reduces uncertainty before interconnecting the organisations?
options: Treat the smaller company’s controls as automatically equivalent to the buyer’s
Establish shared decision authority and inspect inherited identities, trust and dependencies
Connect first and defer asset discovery until after the merger
explanations: Corporate ownership does not establish control equivalence.
Explicit authority and dependency discovery make the integration risk assessable.
Connecting before discovery can introduce unknown trust and administrative paths.

questions.prompt: A service’s confidentiality requirement is satisfied, but corrupted control commands can still alter a process. Which conclusion is supported?
options: Confidentiality evidence alone does not establish command integrity or authorised action
Encryption always establishes the correctness of the process command
Availability is the only relevant property because the system is OT
explanations: Security properties address different failure modes and require separate requirements and tests.
Encryption can protect transit while an authorised or compromised endpoint originates a harmful command.
OT priorities follow consequence; integrity and authority may be crucial.

questions.prompt: Which exception record elements establish continuing accountability? Select all that apply.
options: An expiry or scheduled review and revocation triggers
A named accountable owner
The affected scope and residual-risk decision
A permanent waiver of all related logging
explanations: Time and event conditions prevent unchecked continuation.
The owner is responsible for decisions and closure.
Scope and an explicit decision identify what exposure was accepted.
Removing all related evidence impairs accountability rather than establishing it.

questions.prompt: A firm adopts a recognised control catalogue. What must still be established before claiming the service meets its requirements?
options: Only that the catalogue is widely used
That every control in the catalogue is implemented identically
The applicable scope, tailoring, implementation and assessed effectiveness
explanations: Popularity does not connect controls to this service’s risks or evidence.
Tailoring and applicability matter; indiscriminate identical implementation can be inappropriate.
A catalogue is a source of candidates, not proof of relevant effective deployment.

questions.prompt: A security committee repeatedly approves work but nobody can accept residual service risk. What should governance clarify first?
options: Whether the committee's recommendation automatically binds every service owner
Whether implementation access can substitute for delegated business-risk authority
The accountable risk owner and the authority delegated to each decision body
explanations: Incorrect. Recommendation and risk-acceptance authority must be explicitly assigned; neither can be presumed from meeting participation.
Incorrect. Technical privileges do not confer authority to accept residual business exposure.
The missing decision right blocks valid acceptance regardless of technical activity.

questions.prompt: A divested business retains access through the parent company’s identity federation. What evidence establishes effective separation?
options: An attempted old-trust access is denied and the relevant trust configuration is reconciled
The divested users no longer appear in the parent's ordinary employee search
The sale agreement has been signed
explanations: Configuration plus a negative test addresses the residual access path.
Incorrect. Directory presentation can change while federation, tokens or application rights remain effective.
Legal ownership transfer does not automatically remove technical trust.

questions.prompt: Security staff identify a credible defect involving sensitive customer records. Which approach best preserves both truthful reporting and confidentiality?
options: Use the authorised escalation process, restrict evidence access and obtain appropriate guidance on conflicting duties
Publish all customer records publicly to demonstrate transparency
Suppress the defect because the records are confidential
explanations: Controlled disclosure preserves the ability to act without unjustified dissemination.
Transparency does not authorise unrestricted release of sensitive evidence.
Confidentiality is not a reason to falsify or conceal material findings from authorised decision makers.

questions.prompt: An encrypted dataset is reused for a new business purpose without an applicability review. What remains unresolved?
options: Whether the new processing purpose is permitted
Whether encryption prevents all data access
Only the choice of encryption algorithm, assuming purpose authorization carries over unchanged
explanations: Security of storage does not establish a lawful or otherwise authorised purpose.
Encryption normally permits authorised decryption and is not the disputed processing decision.
Incorrect. The unresolved review concerns the new use and its applicable authority; encryption choice cannot establish that authority.

questions.prompt: Which evidence most directly challenges a claim that personal data never leaves its selected region?
options: Support bundles containing identifiers are downloaded by staff in another region
The primary database has encryption enabled
The service uses a region-specific hostname
explanations: The support copy is a separate data movement that must be evaluated.
Encryption does not determine where data is processed or accessed.
A hostname does not describe every support and replication path.

questions.prompt: A contract calls a supplier a processor, but the supplier independently chooses new purposes for the data. What should be reviewed?
options: Only the contractual role label without examining the supplier's actual decisions
The actual role and processing arrangement, rather than relying only on its label
Only whether the supplier encrypts the dataset at rest
explanations: Incorrect. The facts about purpose and decision-making can require reassessment of the stated role.
Actual activities and applicable law determine obligations; the label may not reflect the arrangement.
Incorrect. An encryption control does not resolve the supplier's independent choice of data purposes.

questions.prompt: Which statement about consent is appropriate for a GDPR-oriented engineering review?
options: Determine the applicable lawful basis; consent is not the only possible basis
Consent is always mandatory for every organisational data operation
Once consent exists, all future uses and transfers are unrestricted
explanations: The review must identify an applicable basis and the requirements that accompany it.
GDPR recognises other lawful bases; applicability depends on circumstances.
Consent has scope and conditions and does not eliminate other duties.

questions.prompt: An analyst hashes a log export. Which claim is supported by a matching later hash?
options: The source event unquestionably happened exactly as logged
The analyst had legal authority to collect the log
The exported bytes have not changed relative to that reference
explanations: A source can produce false or incomplete records before export.
Authority comes from the applicable process and law, not a hash.
A cryptographic integrity check addresses changes to the digital object.

questions.prompt: An authorised hold covers specified records due for routine deletion. Which implementation is appropriate?
options: Suspend destruction for the scoped records and track the hold and its release
Allow the deletion because the ordinary retention timer is automated
Disable deletion permanently for all organisational data
explanations: Scoped preservation honours the hold while retaining lifecycle discipline.
Automation does not override an applicable preservation obligation.
Indefinite blanket retention creates additional exposure and is not justified by a scoped hold.

questions.prompt: A software package can be downloaded publicly. What can the security team infer about redistribution?
options: Public download implies unrestricted commercial redistribution
Redistribution is always prohibited regardless of licence
The applicable licence still needs review
explanations: Public availability does not waive licence and copyright conditions.
Some licences permit redistribution subject to conditions.
Access to the bits and permission to reuse them are separate questions.

questions.prompt: Which contract provision best supports recovery assurance for an outsourced service?
options: A statement that the supplier uses modern technology
An uptime promise without backup or recovery responsibilities
A defined restore objective, responsibilities, test evidence and remediation process
explanations: Technology age does not establish recovery capability.
Availability commitments alone do not specify data loss or restoration behaviour.
Observable objectives and evidence connect contractual duties to recovery performance.

questions.prompt: A security responder finds suspected criminal conduct on a company device. What should be established before expanding collection?
options: Investigation authority, scope, legal/privacy constraints and preservation process
That any suspicion grants unlimited access to all employee devices
That criminal suspicion cancels chain-of-custody requirements
explanations: Collection must remain authorised and support the appropriate proceedings.
Suspicion does not confer unrestricted legal powers.
Evidence handling remains important and may become more consequential.

questions.prompt: Replacing customer names with stable tokens while retaining a lookup table most directly provides what?
options: Automatic permission to publish the full dataset
Pseudonymisation whose reidentification path still needs protection
Guaranteed irreversible anonymisation
explanations: Tokenisation does not itself authorise disclosure or eliminate inference risk.
The retained mapping can reconnect records to people.
Irreversibility is not established when a lookup remains.

questions.prompt: Which factors belong in a cross-border data assessment? Select all that apply.
options: Applicable roles, purposes and legal transfer requirements
Only the location of the application’s login page
Remote support access and onward recipients
Backup and disaster-recovery copies
explanations: Technical flows need an applicability decision under the relevant obligations.
A login page does not describe the data lifecycle.
Support access can create additional processing paths.
Replicated and retained copies can cross boundaries independently.

questions.prompt: A hosted AI service promises not to train on submitted tickets. Which question remains necessary?
options: How tickets are retained, accessed by support and handled by subprocessors
Whether model outputs are automatically legally accurate
Whether that promise eliminates all need to minimise personal data
explanations: Training use is one purpose; other processing and retention still need review.
A contractual training restriction says nothing about output correctness.
Data minimisation and other requirements are separate.

questions.prompt: A regulatory investigator and an internal HR investigator request the same records. What is the appropriate handling basis?
options: Treat both requests as having identical powers because both are investigations
Verify each request’s authority and scope, then preserve and disclose through the approved process
Delete duplicates so only one investigator can receive evidence
explanations: The word investigation does not establish equivalent authority.
Different proceedings can have different powers and disclosure conditions.
Destroying records to simplify requests can undermine preservation duties.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion about a recognised technical standard is defensible?
options: Its mandatory status depends on applicable law, contract or governance adoption
A private contract can always override a conflicting statutory duty
Every published standard is mandatory in every jurisdiction
explanations: A standard can become binding through a particular source of authority and scope.
Private agreement does not provide a universal exemption from law.
Publication alone does not create universal legal force.

questions.prompt: What is the annualised loss expectancy under the supplied simplified model?
options: USD 2,500,000 per year
USD 300,000 per year
USD 36,000 per year
explanations: Dividing loss by frequency reverses the expected-loss calculation.
This is the single-event loss, without frequency.
Multiply loss per event by annual frequency: 300,000 × 0.12.
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic training exhibit; no live system or actual organisation was tested.

Estimated loss per event: USD 300,000. Expected event frequency: 0.12 per year.

questions.prompt: What is the simple annual net benefit of the proposed control?
explanations: This is the gross expected reduction before the control cost.
This is residual ALE, not net benefit.
Expected reduction is 36,000−9,000=27,000; subtract annual cost 20,000.
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic training exhibit; no live system or actual organisation was tested.

Current ALE USD 36,000/year. Projected residual ALE USD 9,000/year. Annual control cost USD 20,000. Ignore initial costs for this calculation.

questions.prompt: An analyst reports ARO=2.4. Is that inherently invalid?
options: No; an annual event frequency can exceed one when repeated events are possible
Yes; every frequency must lie between zero and one
No; it means each event causes a 240% loss
explanations: ARO can represent an expected count of events/year rather than a single-event probability.
The zero-to-one bound applies to probabilities, not arbitrary event counts.
Frequency and fraction lost are different model inputs.

questions.prompt: Two scenarios have identical ALE. Which additional fact could justify prioritising one?
options: One has a catastrophic credible loss exceeding the organisation’s tolerance
Both estimates use the same annual reporting period
Both scenarios received the same ordinal risk-matrix score
explanations: Expected value can conceal a tail consequence that violates tolerance.
Incorrect. A common time basis supports comparison but does not itself justify prioritizing one equal-ALE scenario.
Incorrect. Equal scores do not expose differences in tail consequences, constraints or uncertainty that could justify priority.

questions.prompt: A mitigation is designed but has not been deployed. How should a current risk assessment treat it?
options: Remove the risk from the register because funding exists
Reduce current risk as soon as the purchase order is signed
Separate current residual risk from projected post-treatment risk
explanations: An approved treatment plan does not eliminate current exposure.
Procurement evidence does not establish operational effectiveness.
Current controls and future assumptions must not be conflated.

questions.prompt: Why is multiplying the two path-unavailability probabilities unsupported here?
options: Probabilities can never be multiplied in reliability analysis
The shared power dependency violates the assumed independence
Two routes always fail together regardless of design
explanations: Multiplication can be valid under appropriate independent or conditional models.
A common-cause event can dominate total unavailability and requires its own model.
Failure correlation depends on actual shared dependencies, not merely the route count.
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic training exhibit; no live system or actual organisation was tested.

Path A and B each have estimated unavailability 0.01 in a defined interval. Both depend on one power supply. The calculation uses 0.01×0.01 as total unavailability.

questions.prompt: A risk matrix assigns scores 12 and 6. What can be claimed without further calibration?
options: The adopted method ranks or groups the scenarios; a twofold real-world risk ratio is not established
The first necessarily happens twice as often
The first necessarily has twice the expected financial loss
explanations: Ordinal category arithmetic does not automatically have ratio-scale meaning.
Impact and likelihood ranks cannot be interpreted as event frequencies without calibration.
The score may combine nonfinancial categories and does not measure dollars.

questions.prompt: Which evidence most directly tests a proposed reduction in ransomware recovery loss?
options: A restore exercise meets the data-loss and service-restoration objectives using isolated recovery material
The backup software licence has been renewed
The latest backup job reports a successful start
explanations: Measured restoration addresses recoverability and the consequence model.
Licensing is not a recovery test.
Starting a job does not establish usable backup contents or service recovery.

questions.prompt: An insurance policy covers some interruption costs. Which conclusion is appropriate?
options: The policy prevents the triggering technical failure
Covered financial loss may be shared while operational and other residual consequences remain
All risk is eliminated once premiums are paid
explanations: Insurance is not a preventive technical control.
Risk transfer is limited by coverage, exclusions and consequences that cannot be transferred.
The insured service can still fail and claims can be limited.

questions.prompt: An organisation has no recorded incidents but weak detection. What is the defensible use of this history?
options: Treat it as incomplete observation and examine detection coverage and other evidence
Conclude threat likelihood is zero
Assume every undiscovered event was catastrophic
explanations: An absence of records can reflect an observation gap; neither extreme inference is justified.
No detections do not prove no events.
Missing observations do not establish maximum consequences.

questions.prompt: Which change should trigger risk reassessment before the annual review?
options: The same scenario is reviewed by a new analyst without any change in assumptions or evidence
The unchanged risk register is printed again
A critical service moves onto a newly shared identity dependency
explanations: Incorrect. A personnel change alone is not the substantive risk change sought in this question.
Reprinting unchanged information does not introduce new risk evidence.
A dependency change can alter common-cause exposure and recovery assumptions.

questions.prompt: A financial model compares one year of expected loss reduction with five years of control cost. What needs correction?
options: Always delete recurring costs from the model
Put costs and benefits on a common horizon using the approved valuation method
Multiply both amounts by the impact rank
explanations: Recurring costs are real decision inputs and cannot be discarded.
Comparable cash-flow timing is necessary for a meaningful economic comparison.
An ordinal rank does not fix inconsistent financial horizons.

questions.prompt: Which statements describe an informed risk acceptance? Select all that apply.
options: The decision records assumptions and review triggers
Acceptance stays within applicable constraints and authority
A defined residual exposure is reviewed by a delegated owner
Unfunded remediation silently remains in a backlog
explanations: Assumptions and triggers make continued acceptance reviewable.
The owner cannot waive obligations beyond their authority.
The owner must know what risk is retained and have authority.
Neglect or deferral without an authorised decision is not informed acceptance.

questions.prompt: A proposed monitoring control records attacks but nobody receives or investigates alerts. Which assumed benefit is least supported?
options: Increased availability of raw event records
The ability to retain events for later analysis if storage works
Reduced incident loss through faster response
explanations: Raw collection may still work even though operational response is missing.
Retained records can support later analysis, but this is different from timely response.
Without a functioning response path, recording does not establish faster containment or reduced consequence.

questions.prompt: Which missing flow most weakens this threat model?
options: The privileged logic-upload path from engineering laptop to controller
A second description of an already modeled telemetry path with unchanged trust and authority
An additional inventory entry for a component whose relevant flows are already modeled
explanations: The upload changes process behaviour and crosses an authority boundary omitted from the model.
Incorrect. Restating an existing flow does not address the omitted boundary in the exhibit.
Incorrect. Inventory detail alone does not expose the missing flow and its trust transition.
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic training exhibit; no live system or actual organisation was tested.

The diagram includes controller-to-historian telemetry and operator viewing. Engineers also upload logic over a maintenance connection, which is not shown.

questions.prompt: A controller accepts a correctly signed but prohibited old firmware release. Which control property is missing?
options: Verification that a recognised key signed the bytes
Version acceptability and rollback enforcement
Detection of accidental corruption in transit
explanations: The scenario states signature verification succeeds; additional signature repetition does not establish version policy.
Signature verification alone does not enforce the minimum acceptable release.
A valid signature over the received artifact can already detect alteration; the issue is authorised old content.

questions.prompt: What additional evidence is needed to connect an SBOM to the running service?
options: Only the SBOM's publication date without artifact or deployment linkage
Only that the SBOM is signed by the supplier, without identifying the deployed artifact
Reconciliation of deployed artifact identity/version with the SBOM’s declared build
explanations: Incorrect. A recent document can still describe a different build or configuration.
Incorrect. Document authenticity does not establish that it describes the running service.
Component transparency must refer to the actual deployed artifact.

questions.prompt: An attack tree requires both a stolen credential and reachable maintenance interface. Which relationship expresses that path?
options: A sequence that assumes interface reachability cannot change
AND between the two required conditions
OR because either condition always completes the attack
explanations: An attack tree condition should represent reachability, not assume it permanently.
Both preconditions are required for the declared path.
Either alone is insufficient under the stated scenario.

questions.prompt: Two suppliers share the same identity service. Which test most directly examines the claimed supplier independence?
options: Compare the suppliers’ contract renewal dates
Shut down one supplier’s nonproduction web frontend only
Exercise loss of that shared identity dependency and observe both services and their approved fallback
explanations: Separate contracts and dates do not establish operational independence.
A single frontend failure does not exercise the common authentication dependency.
The shared dependency can defeat both paths and must be in the failure experiment.

questions.prompt: A retrieved maintenance document tells an AI assistant to approve a configuration change. Which control best addresses the authority boundary?
options: Trust the instruction because the document was retrieved over TLS
Grant the retrieval component the same privileges as the change approver
Treat retrieved text as untrusted data and require independent scoped authorisation for the change
explanations: TLS protects transport but does not make embedded instructions authoritative.
Conflating retrieval and approval broadens the exact trust-boundary problem.
Content access does not confer authority to approve consequential tool actions.

questions.prompt: A supplier’s component vulnerability is listed in the SBOM. What should determine operational treatment priority?
options: Only whether the component has the newest available upstream version
Affected deployed version, reachable use, consequences and available mitigations
The vulnerability count alone regardless of deployment
explanations: Incorrect. Treatment depends on deployed reachability, exploitability, impact and support; version order alone is insufficient.
Applicability and consequence connect a component finding to an actual risk scenario.
Counts without context can misprioritise unreachable and critical exposures.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly limits a firmware root-of-trust claim?
options: Its assurance depends on what is measured or verified and how trusted references and responses are managed
It proves every application input is safe once the machine boots
It removes the need to control firmware update authority
explanations: A root anchors specified verification properties, not arbitrary system correctness.
Application behaviour lies beyond a boot measurement alone.
An attacker controlling permitted update authority can undermine the trusted state.

questions.prompt: A threat model was approved before emergency remote support was added. What is the appropriate next step?
options: Review the new access path, authority, dependencies and tests in the model
Retain the prior model unchanged because approval is permanent
Retain the earlier trust-boundary analysis because the physical endpoint did not change
explanations: A new trust path can materially change threats even without new hardware.
Models require review when assumptions change.
Incorrect. New remote access can change flows, authority and attack paths without changing the asset.

questions.prompt: Which procurement requirement is most directly testable?
options: Use reputable suppliers for all updates
Provide best-in-class supply-chain security
Reject updates outside the approved release identity and minimum-version policy
explanations: Reputation is a selection input but not a complete acceptance test.
An unmeasured superlative does not define the required behaviour.
It defines observable allow/deny behaviour tied to an explicit policy.

questions.prompt: Which evidence can support supplier assurance without proving it alone? Select all that apply.
options: A scoped SBOM
Reviewed build provenance
A successful signature check
The supplier’s marketing claim that compromise is impossible
explanations: An SBOM contributes component information but needs deployment and completeness checks.
Provenance supports origin/build claims under its trust assumptions.
Signature verification supports signer/byte integrity, not complete safety.
An absolute marketing assertion is not technical evidence of impossibility.

questions.prompt: A model-training dataset is altered by an authorised ingestion account. Why does encryption at rest fail to prevent this mechanism?
options: Encrypted storage cannot ever support integrity controls
The dataset must be publicly readable for poisoning to occur
The attack uses an authorised processing path after permitted decryption
explanations: Integrity controls can coexist with encryption; this control is simply insufficient alone.
Poisoning can occur through privileged or supply-chain paths without public read access.
Storage encryption does not validate the semantic integrity of every authorised input.

questions.prompt: Which supplier-exit evidence best establishes removal of technical trust?
options: The supplier promises to close access at a later unspecified time
Revoked credentials and federation paths are tested, and remaining data/evidence duties are reconciled
The commercial relationship is closed while existing tokens and federation sessions remain untested
explanations: An unbounded promise is not observed closure.
Measured revocation and lifecycle reconciliation address the actual residual dependencies.
Incorrect. Commercial closure does not demonstrate removal of effective technical access.

questions.prompt: A signed update contains malicious code because the build service was compromised. Which additional assurance boundary should be strengthened?
options: Build integrity and the policy controlling what may be signed and released
Only the download channel’s packet checksum
Only the release-signature verification performed at download
explanations: A signature can faithfully authenticate malicious build output; release/build trust must be protected.
Transport checks do not detect an authorised malicious source artifact.
Incorrect. A compromised build can produce a correctly signed malicious artifact; the upstream build/provenance boundary remains relevant.

questions.prompt: Which information is the primary output of a business impact analysis?
options: Required business functions, time-dependent interruption consequences and recovery needs
A list of exploitable software flaws ranked by CVSS alone
A record of packets observed during a penetration test
explanations: BIA defines business consequence and continuity needs.
Vulnerability assessment informs risk but does not establish business interruption tolerances.
Traffic evidence can inform an analysis but is not the BIA’s primary output.

questions.prompt: Has the data-loss objective been demonstrated by the latest verified recovery point?
options: No; the verified point is 50 minutes before failure
Yes; the restore process is expected to take under 30 minutes
Yes; jobs are scheduled every 15 minutes
explanations: Usable point age is 14:00−13:10=50 minutes, beyond the 30-minute RPO.
Restore duration concerns RTO, not the age of recovered data.
Schedule does not establish usable backup results.
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic training exhibit; no live system or actual organisation was tested.

Failure 14:00; RPO30 minutes; backup schedule 15 minutes; latest verified usable consistent point 13:10.

questions.prompt: What is the earliest recovery completion under the stated dependencies?
options: 6 hours
8 hours
10 hours
explanations: This uses the shorter identity path and ignores the database prerequisite.
The critical path is network 3 + database 4 + application 1.
This would add identity and database sequentially despite available parallel resources.
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic training exhibit; no live system or actual organisation was tested.

Network 3 h. Identity 2 h after network. Database 4 h after network. Application 1 h after both. Sufficient independent staff/resources allow parallel identity/database restoration.

questions.prompt: The same specialist must now complete identity restoration before database restoration. What happens to the earlier 8-hour plan?
options: It becomes 6 hours because identity is the smaller task
It becomes 10 hours unless the resource constraint is changed
It remains 8 hours because logical tasks still have separate names
explanations: The database work cannot be omitted.
Resource serialisation produces 3+2+4+1=10 hours.
Nominal logical parallelism does not remove a shared specialist constraint.
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic training exhibit; no live system or actual organisation was tested.

Network 3 h; identity 2 h; database 4 h; application 1 h. Application needs identity and database; one specialist performs the identity and database tasks sequentially.

questions.prompt: Which recovery result meets the stated 8-hour business interruption limit?
options: None;1.5 h decision+5 h restore+2 h reconciliation totals 8.5 h
The 5 h restore alone meets the complete business limit
The 2 h reconciliation can be ignored because servers are reachable
explanations: The declared business clock includes all required work from disruption to acceptable service.
Technical restore is only one component of the total interruption.
Reachability does not finish required business-state reconciliation.
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic training exhibit; no live system or actual organisation was tested.

Business clock begins at disruption. Decision delay 1.5 h. Technical restore 5 h. Required reconciliation 2 h. Maximum tolerable interruption 8 h.

questions.prompt: Why might a low-profile infrastructure service be restored before the highest-priority application?
options: Low-profile systems always have higher business priority
Restoring more small servers is the objective regardless of service function
The application depends on it for authentication or another required function
explanations: Its early position can arise from dependency, not a universal priority rule.
Counting restarted servers does not establish restored business capability.
Dependency-aware sequencing serves the business objective.

questions.prompt: What is the backlog after 3 hours in the supplied manual-workaround case?
options: 165 requests
390 requests
225 requests
explanations: This counts processed requests and omits arrivals and initial queue.
This adds arrivals but ignores completed manual work.
Initial 120 plus net growth(90−55)×3=225.
questions.exhibit:
Synthetic training exhibit; no live system or actual organisation was tested.

Initial queue 120. Arrival 90/hour. Manual processing 55/hour. Rates constant for 3 hours.

questions.prompt: A near-zero-lag replica contains the same malicious deletion as production. What property has not been established?
options: That the replica follows the primary data changes
That changes replicate quickly
An independently usable clean recovery point
explanations: Following the damaging change is exactly the observed problem.
The scenario is consistent with low lag; speed is not the missing claim.
Fast replication is not protection against replicated corruption or deletion.

questions.prompt: Which result can a tabletop exercise directly support?
options: A physical failover completed within measured millisecond limits
The alternate database sustained production transaction volume
Participants identified a missing declaration authority and revised escalation roles
explanations: A discussion cannot measure a physical switching event.
Load performance needs an executed technical test with appropriate workload.
Discussion can expose decision and coordination defects.

questions.prompt: Which recovery dependency requires an explicit bootstrap design?
options: Two tasks have different owners and no shared resources
The key service needs the directory, while the directory backup needs that key service
The application starts after a fully independent network service
explanations: Independence does not create the specified circular blockage.
The circular dependency can block recovery unless an authorised independent path exists.
A simple acyclic prerequisite can be scheduled normally.

questions.prompt: Which evidence is needed before declaring a cyber recovery successful? Select all that apply.

questions.prompt: Which elements belong in role-based learning? Select all that apply.
options: Feedback and later recall or reassessment
Guided practice followed by a varied independent task
Tasks and consequences relevant to the role
Identical practical depth for all roles regardless of duties
explanations: Feedback and spaced retrieval help identify and address gaps.
Progression supports skill acquisition and transfer.
The objective should follow required behaviour and risk.
Uniform depth can miss specialist needs and waste effort on irrelevant tasks.

options: Two approvals do not establish independent examination of the underlying evidence

Any two approvals automatically prove the change is safe

Approval does not replace technical validation.
Safety requires appropriate evidence and authority, not merely two signatures.

questions.prompt: Which personnel-screening principle is appropriate for a privileged role?
options: Treat a successful initial check as permanent proof of trustworthy behaviour
Apply every available intrusive check regardless of relevance or authority
Use relevant proportionate checks under applicable law and policy, then maintain lifecycle controls
explanations: People and circumstances change; one check cannot guarantee future conduct.
Role relevance and legal authority constrain collection and processing.
Screening is a bounded risk input and must be combined with ongoing controls.

questions.prompt: A security champion is asked to approve risks outside their delegated authority. What should the programme do?

Treat the champion title as unlimited risk acceptance authority
Clarify the champion’s support/escalation role and route acceptance to the authorised owner

Titles do not replace explicit delegation.
A liaison role does not automatically confer accountable decision rights.

questions.prompt: A public status feed drives a consequential operational decision. Which protection requirement follows?

Treat encryption at rest as sufficient for all relying decisions
Apply the highest confidentiality class solely because it is operational
Assess integrity, freshness and availability separately from disclosure permission

A public confidentiality class does not settle other security properties.

questions.prompt: Who should authorise declassification of an information asset under the stated governance model?
options: The first recipient of an exported copy

The accountable information owner using the approved policy
Any storage administrator with permission to edit its tag
explanations: Receipt does not transfer classification authority.
Operational custody does not automatically confer declassification authority.
The owner holds the classification decision right under policy.
Technical ability to change metadata is not governance authority.

questions.prompt: Which inventory discrepancy is least likely to be resolved by passive network observation alone?

A powered-off replacement server stored for recovery
An active switch sending discovery traffic
explanations: Observed connections can reveal presence, though ownership still needs reconciliation.

An inactive spare produces no network traffic and needs other inventory evidence.
An observed active device can contribute network evidence.

questions.prompt: A restricted dataset becomes publicly shared after CSV export. What is the primary control gap?

The original database’s access rules automatically govern every exported file

The derived copy needs an approved label and enforced handling.
Format conversion is not a sanitisation or declassification process.

questions.prompt: An encrypted database is queried by an authorised process that logs full records. Which data state creates the additional exposure?
options: In-use processing and its newly created log copies
Only the encrypted source volume before the authorised query
Only the original encrypted-at-rest state
No state, because authorisation makes every subsequent use acceptable
explanations: Decrypted processing can produce sensitive outputs requiring their own controls.

The new plaintext or sensitive log copy is outside the original storage protection boundary.
Authorisation is scoped to purpose and actions; it is not unrestricted reuse.

questions.prompt: A combined dataset reveals access patterns that individual records did not reveal. What should happen?
options: Assume aggregation always reduces sensitivity
Assess the derivative’s consequence and classify its combined information
Inherit the lowest input label without further review
Discard lineage because only the final dataset matters
explanations: Aggregation can either reduce or increase exposure depending on the result.
Combination can create new inference and disclosure consequences.
The least restrictive input does not determine the derivative’s risk.
Lineage is needed to understand and govern the derived content.

questions.prompt: Which pairing correctly distinguishes an information owner from a custodian?

Owner sets authorised use/classification; custodian implements approved handling
Owner performs every backup; custodian alone accepts business loss
Custodian determines all privacy purposes simply by storing the data
explanations: Roles can be combined but are not required to be identical.
Accountability for use and implementation of handling are distinct responsibilities.
Backup execution and risk acceptance cannot be assigned solely by this reversed label.
Storage responsibility does not automatically determine processing purposes.

questions.prompt: A DLP system sees web uploads but not an application’s direct export API. Which conclusion is supported?
options: The web-upload test also proves API policy enforcement

The API export must be safe because web uploads are inspected
explanations: Different enforcement paths require relevant tests.
A coverage gap does not negate useful controls on observed channels.
Coverage must be assessed per actual path and integration.
Safety of an unobserved channel cannot be inferred from another.

questions.prompt: Which new service asset most clearly needs inventory treatment despite lacking a physical serial number?

A discarded transient copy of public information with no continuing service dependency

explanations: Incorrect. The stem asks for a consequential service asset; this preference has no stated service role.

questions.prompt: Which statement about embeddings is defensible?

Vector conversion proves all personal information is irrecoverable
Removing direct identifiers from retrieval metadata guarantees the embeddings cannot expose sensitive relationships
Embeddings inherit public status regardless of source restrictions
explanations: Transformation alone does not establish a universal privacy guarantee.
Irrecoverability requires evidence under a specified threat model.
Incorrect. Embedding content and auxiliary information can retain consequential information despite metadata minimization.
Source purpose, contractual restrictions and derived content still matter.

questions.prompt: Which action is legitimate baseline tailoring?

Use the word tailored to bypass the risk owner’s review
Remove a difficult control without recording its residual exposure
Apply only controls already supported by purchased tools
explanations: Tailoring is a controlled applicability and parameter decision.
A label does not confer waiver authority.
An undocumented removal leaves an unmanaged requirement gap.
Tool capability does not determine the full required protection.

questions.prompt: Which lifecycle event should trigger classification review?

Its stable identifier is displayed in a different approved inventory view
Its unchanged classification label is rendered in a new approved reporting format
explanations: A compliant unchanged copy does not necessarily change classification, though handling still applies.
New purpose and recipients can change obligations and consequence.
Inventory display does not change the asset’s use or consequence.
Incorrect. A presentation-only change does not alter the data, purpose, access or impact that drives classification review.

questions.prompt: Which facts should a decision-oriented asset inventory include? Select all that apply.
options: Accountable owner and purpose

Dependencies and lifecycle/support state
Only purchase price and the count of devices
explanations: These identify who decides and why the asset exists.
These support handling and applicability decisions.
These support continuity, vulnerability and retirement decisions.
Cost and count alone omit consequential intangible and operational facts.

questions.prompt: A DRM-protected document is opened by a supported reader, but an allowed output channel exports unrestricted text. What should assurance examine?
options: Only whether the original document was encrypted
The actual usage and output enforcement boundary
Only whether the document label remains visible in the supported reader
Only whether the recipient authenticated successfully before opening the document
explanations: Encryption of the original does not govern every authorised output.
DRM claims depend on enforced reader and output behaviour.
Incorrect. A displayed restriction does not establish enforcement on the allowed export channel.

questions.prompt: A backup container is marked internal, but it includes restricted keys and customer exports. What should determine handling?
options: Only the container’s generic default label
Only the parent container's inherited default classification
The contained information and applicable protection requirements
The sensitivity of the least restricted file
explanations: Defaults can be wrong and need reconciliation.
Incorrect. A generic inherited label must be reconciled with the actual more-sensitive contents.
Container handling must account for the protected contents and policy.
Least-restrictive handling can expose more sensitive contents.

questions.prompt: A new cloud asset is provisioned with no owner and no retention rule. What should be corrected before routine use?

Provider infrastructure responsibility does not automatically transfer business data ownership.

Secure provisioning includes ownership, protection and lifecycle requirements.

Only a successful authorised download
Only confirmation that every source object has a classification label

Masking changes returned representation; authorisation decides permitted access or action

questions.prompt: An AI assistant’s generated text says a user is authorised to change production. What should the change system rely on?

The presence of an administrator title in the prompt

It makes media-specific method selection unnecessary

It must have physically failed
Its security updates continue automatically because it still runs

Records reconcile all 24 media identities to suitable methods, results and acceptance

Return the device to unrestricted reuse because it is unreadable by the host
Keep controlled custody and use an approved alternative after assessing the failure

It can be accepted on flash solely because the same method was approved for a magnetic drive

Only the physical durability of the retained storage media

That the API returned the documented request status
That the delete request was issued
That the tenant’s normal volume reference disappeared

Remove application disks and assume all credentials elsewhere vanish

Validation means ignoring media identity if a tool returns success
Validation is only repeating the tool's success query without considering the intended disposition
Validation removes the need for an authorised disposition

Copy the key to an unmanaged personal device and declare it erased

The birthday bound gives an exponent near half the digest bits.
